title: "Surfing Einstein – The Discovery of Gravitational Waves: Where Science Meets Dance"
excerpt: pattern library e styleguide per Unina
content:
On Wednesday, October 14, 2026 , at the Teatro dei Piccoli at the Mostra d’Oltremare in Naples , “Surfing Einstein – The Discovery of Gravitational Waves: Between Science and Dance” will take place, a cultural and scientific event that offers an original fusion of physics, film, and dance.

The initiative is sponsored by the “All’Ombra del Cervo di Rodi” APS Association and the Oltremarigliano APS Association, as part of the “Philosophy Festival – MAPFFEST in itinere,” under the patronage of the City of Naples and with the participation of the “Ettore Pancini” Department of Physics at the University of Naples Federico II, the INFN – Naples Section, the VIRGO Naples group, and the Teatro dei Piccoli – Le Nuvole.

The highlight of the event will be the screening of *Surfing Einstein*, an artistic documentary by director and choreographer Meritxell Campos Olivé, which uses an original language of images, music, and dance to tell the story of one of the most important achievements in contemporary physics: the discovery of gravitational waves.

​​​​​Thefilm’sprotagonistsare the scientists of the VIRGO project themselves, who perform a choreography that, alongside the scientific research, conveys the passion, perseverance, and human dimension of the scientists’ work.

Two screenings are scheduled, both with free admission: at 10:00 a.m., specifically for high school students, and at 6:30 p.m., open to the general public.

Meritxell Campos Olivé and physicists from VIRGO Naples will be present during the screenings to provide in-depth scientific explanations and engage in dialogue with the audience. A model of the VIRGO interferometer in Cascina will also be on display, providing an accessible explanation of how the instrument works and the role of interferometry in gravitational wave research.

The initiative aims, in particular, to engage young people with scientific research through a narrative that bridges science and art, while also highlighting the creativity, passion, and collaborative spirit that characterize research.
